    People also ask
    Is holistic dentistry legitimate?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, holistic dentistry is considered a legitimate, alternative approach to dental care when practiced by licensed DDS or DMD professionals who prioritize biocompatible materials and whole-body health. While they are qualified dentists, the field itself is not a recognized specialty, and some practices (e.g., removing mercury fillings or questioning root canals) may lack strong scientific evidence. 
    Key Aspects of Holistic Dentistry: 
    • Licensing: Holistic or biological dentists have the same foundational education and licenses as traditional dentists.
    • Approach: They focus on how oral health connects to the whole body, often using "natural" or biocompatible materials (e.g., avoiding mercury/amalgam fillings)
      .
    • Prevention: Emphasizes long-term preventative care and nutrition to prevent gum disease and cavities.
    • Concerns/Controversies: Some practitioners may promote procedures that are not scientifically validated, such as removing mercury fillings to cure unrelated illnesses. 
    How to Choose:
    If you prefer a focus on natural products, biocompatible materials, and a more conservative approach, a holistic dentist may be a good option. However, it is advisable to ensure they base their treatments on evidence-based dentistry and that their practices align with safe, conventional methods.
